column1: # Books worth keeping a copy of: documents fetched from where they are published into
# the shared books folder, each one checked against the checksum recorded here.
# Columns, separated by single tabs: id, shelf (a folder beneath media/books), address,
# SHA-256 of the file, size in bytes, rights, title (40 characters at most), note.
#   offline books                            what is listed, and what is already here
#   sudo offline books get outdoor-cooking   every book on that shelf
# A file that is not the size and checksum recorded here is discarded, whichever
# machine served it, so a line vouches for exactly one file. Some of these are the
# Internet Archive's own PDF of a scanned book, which the Archive may one day
# regenerate; that book will then fail its check until its line is brought up to date.
# The rights column says what stands behind each line:
#   pd      in the public domain, by age or as the work of a government
#   cc      under a Creative Commons licence given by its author or editor
#   marked  marked as free to copy by the person who placed it in the Internet Archive,
#           which could not be confirmed from the document itself. Treat it, like any
#           private-use line, as a copy for your own household and not for passing on.
# Put your own in /etc/offline/books.local.tsv using the same layout. There alone the
# checksum and size may each be a single hyphen, for a file whose checksum you have no
# means of knowing beforehand; such a file is checked for its type and nothing more.
